audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read 'Skill' for all seven rows while the content layer and the packet's levelChart both read LeBlanc/LeBlanc/LeBlanc/LeBlanc/Katarina/LeBlanc/Katarina. Six rows rendered two different answers.
audit.why: The content chart is the defensible one and it matches the packet. LeBlanc's E reaches 925 against Shunpo's 725 and her Q is 700 against a 625 Bouncing Blade, so pre-6 she controls spacing. Level 6 and the late game go to Katarina: Death Lotus plus Voracity's cooldown refund off any nearby death.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> LeBlanc (6/10), phases[4].side -> Katarina (4/10), phases[5].side -> LeBlanc, phases[6].side -> Katarina (4/10), with every why rewritten to argue its row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was credited to 'Death Lotus resets on kill'. Death Lotus does not reset; Voracity does, and it triggers on any champion dying that Katarina damaged recently — including a teammate's kill.
audit.why: Enemy passive text: 'Whenever an enemy champion dies that Katarina has damaged recently, her remaining ability cooldowns are dramatically reduced.' Enemy R text carries no reset clause.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1], mid and dontsFull[2].d now credit Voracity and carry Death Lotus's real 75/60/45s cooldown and 550 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death Lotus is a channel and nothing on the page said so. Ethereal Chains — or a mimicked Ethereal Chains — cancels it outright, which is the single highest-value interaction in this matchup and was absent from all fifteen report entries and every breakdown field.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule channel-interruptible; enemy R text: 'becomes a flurry of blades... while she channels'.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d, phases[4].why, whys[5], spikes[1] and mid all now tell you to hold E for the channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and pointed at Shunpo as the punishable window. Shunpo costs no mana and is 12s down to 8s — she is essentially never without it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to point at the real window — no dagger on the ground — plus the 75s Death Lotus.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] named 'Sinister Steel (W)'. Katarina's W is Preparation. Eleven fields also called her he/his, and two bullets were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Enemy kit W is Preparation; champ-gender lists Katarina as she/her; lintFindings enumerates every field.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name replaced, all MISGENDER fields regendered, both bleed bullets rewritten with kit-grounded bodies.

notes: The content chart matched the packet levelChart, so the full layer's all-Skill chart was the wrong half and was moved to match — win[] needed no edits. The kit file tags Bouncing Blade with a 'grounding' flag and Preparation with a 'knockup' flag; Riot's descriptions for both say nothing of the kind, so per the brief's rule I trusted the descriptions and wrote neither. Whether Death Lotus's channel survives LeBlanc's E shackle (before the 1.5s root) or only breaks on the root itself is not answerable from the kit text — I wrote that the chain cancels it, which the missingInteractions rule asserts directly.
